$comment: What a release of this workspace contains, and what it is built against.
Read by .github/workflows/ci.yml. Kept as an explicit file rather than
inferred from folder names, because the two decisions below are product
decisions and must be visible in a diff when they change.
$comment_platformImage: The ZuloOne image the bundles are exported BY, pinned rather than 'newest'.
A bundle is produced by importing this workspace into a running ZuloOne and
exporting each model back out, so the platform version is part of how the
artifact was made. Pinning it makes a rebuild of the same tag reproducible,
and records what a package was tested against — which matters once a model
declares a MinVersion on Core, since Core's version IS the platform's.
localhost:5000, NOT 10.10.0.210:5000, and the difference is not cosmetic.
The registry serves plain HTTP; Docker treats localhost as insecure by
default but refuses any other host without an insecure-registries entry.
The CI host has none, so the LAN address fails with 'server gave HTTP
response to HTTPS client'. This file is read only by CI, which runs on that
host, so the loopback name is the correct one here — tenants reach the same
registry by its LAN address because their host is configured for it.
$comment_platformPin: The pin must be a platform that can INSTALL THE TREE, not merely run.
2026.0.93 could not: it predates event Chain of Command. Handlers call
next() (ZOCOC001); that method is not on EventHandlerBase until 2026.0.104
(platform run 104, commit 3780ba76). Compiling this tree on .93 is CS0103
in Common and TestBench, then DependencyFailed for everyone else.
TypedTablePartEventHandler arrived after 114 (platform run 120, live field
eval). Line handlers in this tree declare that base; compiling them on .114
is CS0246 in Accounting, then DependencyFailed for everyone else.
[ExtensionOf] / ExtensionOfAttribute and owner-exempt ZOCOC001 arrived at
platform run 130 (commit 7e7744c8). Cross-model handlers in this tree
declare the attribute; compiling them on .120 is CS0246 in CRM and Costing.
TBWarehouseEvents dropped next() as link 0; the .120 analyzer still demanded
So the order is fixed and one-way: a platform that reads what CI writes
reaches the registry FIRST, this pin moves to it SECOND, and only then may
the tree change shape. Bumping this line before the platform exists ships
an image whose tenants boot healthy with no business layer.
$comment_exclude: Models with NO bundle exported for them.
TestBench and TestBenchExt are fixtures for the in-app integration tests —
together the densest folders in the tree (169 files) and indistinguishable
from business models at the directory level. They must still be imported
during the build, because the tests that prove the workspace works live in
them; they simply must not be published.
Core is here for a mechanical reason: ModelBundleService.ExportAsync throws
on a system model, so no Core bundle can be produced at all. That is not the
same as Core not being shipped — see treeExclude below.
The stand customization model is seeded by the platform (layer 4) so jobs
and scripts have somewhere to live before any package lands. Its identity
is fixed; the name is the tenant in PascalCase (or Local on an anonymous
stand). It is not a workspace model. CI also skips it by metaId, so a
rename does not accidentally publish it. Tenant/Local stay here as the
historical names of that same row.
$comment_treeExclude: Models NOT copied into the distribution image's workspace tree.
The tree, not the bundles, is what a tenant now installs from — measured:
the bundle format carries seven kinds of object and the workspace tree
carries seventeen. Number sequences, form layouts, print forms, widgets,
total drivers, link tables, analytics and global constants have no bundle
representation and were being dropped in silence. Common shipped its ten
dictionaries without any of its fourteen number sequences.
Core IS in the tree, and that is the correction. It owns forty-nine form
layouts, fifteen number sequences, five print forms, five total drivers and
three widgets, and nothing else delivered them — ModelSeeder creates the row
and no content. 'Core's version is the application version' remains true and
is why the tenant re-applies Core whenever the platform version moves; it
was never a reason to leave Core's content out of the image.
The fixtures stay out: they are imported during the build as the gate, and
The stand model (Local / Tenant / whatever the tenant renamed it to) is
seeded by the platform on first boot. Shipping it as a workspace tree
makes the catalogue list a package nobody created, and the upgrade gate
then tries to extract it from a release that never had the folder.
